paper_metadata.title: Effects of Chromium on the Microstructures and Mechanical Properties of AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 Eutectic High Entropy Alloys

evidence.quote: In the present study, a series of AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) eutectic high entropy alloys (EHEAs) have been designed and prepared.
For this AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 alloy system, the deformation under room temperature compression was generated by a plastic deformation of the FCC phase.
The fraction of consisted phases and the microstructures will affect the mechanical property of the AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy system.

AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0) alloy ingots (about 35 g) were prepared by using a vacuum arc melting method under argon atmosphere. The AlCoCrxFeNi2.1 alloys with x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0 are denoted as Cr0, Cr0.25, Cr0.5, Cr0.75, and Cr1.0, respectively.

The Cr0 alloy exhibits a hypoeutectic microstructure with a hard B2 primary phase, which leads to a higher yield strength.
The Cr-free AlCoFeNi2.1 alloy exhibited a hypoeutectic, which was composed of a primary phase and lamellar eutectic structure.

Wherein, the Cr0.25 and Cr0.5 alloys exhibited excellent compressive mechanical properties, the yield strengths, fracture strengths, and plastic strains are as high as 617 MPa vs. 617 MPa, 3161 MPa vs. 3167 MPa, and 47.5 vs. 47.6%, respectively.
The Cr0.5 EHEA exhibited excellent tensile mechanical properties, with a yield strength of 536.5 MPa, a fracture strength of 1062 MPa, and an elongation of 13.8%.

However, for the Cr0.25, Cr0.5, Cr0.75, and Cr1.0 alloys, having a eutectic microstructures without hard B2 primary phase exhibited lower yield strength and better compressive ductility will be obtained.
